# Mastra Changelog 2026-02-24 | Mastra Blog

We’ve been busy smoothing out a few of the rough edges that show up once you start running real workloads, long-lived sandboxes, and production UIs. The result is a release that makes workspaces more powerful, more controllable, and easier to debug.

**Release:** `@mastra/core@1.7.0`

Let's dive in:

## [Background Process Management in Workspaces & Sandboxes![](https://mastra.ai/_next/static/immutable/media/anchor.3595n93ztlxu8.svg)](https://mastra.ai/blog/changelog-2026-02-24#background-process-management-in-workspaces-and-sandboxes)

Workspaces can now spawn and manage long-running background processes inside sandbox environments, which is perfect for dev servers, file watchers, background jobs, and REPL-style workflows. Under the hood, core introduces a `SandboxProcessManager` abstraction plus a `ProcessHandle` API for streaming output, waiting on exit, and managing process lifecycle. ([PR #13293](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13293 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13293"))

That matters because previously you had two awkward choices: block on every command until it exits, or build your own process tracking outside the sandbox. Now you can start a process once, keep it running, and inspect or kill it later, all through a consistent sandbox API.

Here’s what it looks like at the sandbox layer:

```
// Spawn a background process
const handle = await sandbox.processes.spawn('node server.js');
 
// Stream output and wait for exit
const result = await handle.wait({
  onStdout: data => console.log(data),
});
 
// List and manage running processes
const procs = await sandbox.processes.list();
await sandbox.processes.kill(handle.pid);
```

A few implementation details you can rely on:

*   `SandboxProcessManager` base class: `spawn()`, `list()`, `get(pid)`, `kill(pid)`
*   `ProcessHandle` base class: stdout/stderr accumulation, streaming callbacks, and `.wait()`
*   `LocalProcessManager` for Node.js, wrapping `child_process`
*   Stream interop via `handle.reader` / `handle.writer`
*   `executeCommand` now has a default implementation built on the process manager (spawn + wait)

On top of that, workspace tooling got first-class support for background processes and a much nicer terminal-style execution display. `execute_command` now supports `background: true`, and there are new tools for inspecting output and terminating processes. ([PR #13309](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13309 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13309"))

```
// Example: start a long-running process from a workspace tool call
await workspace.tools.execute_command({
  command: "npm run dev",
  background: true,
  // returns { pid, ... }
});
 
// Later, check output or block until it exits
await workspace.tools.get_process_output({
  pid: 12345,
  wait: false,
});
 
// Or stop it
await workspace.tools.kill_process({ pid: 12345 });
```

Along the way you also get practical UI improvements like output truncation helpers (tail lines), execution badges that show streaming output and exit codes, killed status, and workspace metadata, all aimed at making sandboxes feel like a real terminal instead of a black box. ([PR #13309](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13309 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13309"))

## [Runtime Tool Configuration Updates via Workspace.setToolsConfig()![](https://mastra.ai/_next/static/immutable/media/anchor.3595n93ztlxu8.svg)](https://mastra.ai/blog/changelog-2026-02-24#runtime-tool-configuration-updates-via-workspacesettoolsconfig)

You can now enable or disable workspace tools dynamically on an existing `Workspace` instance using `Workspace.setToolsConfig()`. Passing `undefined` resets to the default behavior and re-enables all tools. ([PR #13439](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13439 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13439"))

This is a big quality-of-life improvement if you switch modes at runtime, for example “plan only”, “read-only”, tenant-specific restrictions, or progressive enablement after a user confirmation. You no longer need to recreate the workspace (and everything attached to it) just to lock down a couple of capabilities.

```
const workspace = new Workspace({ filesystem, sandbox });
 
// Disable write tools (e.g., in plan/read-only mode)
workspace.setToolsConfig({
  mastra_workspace_write_file: { enabled: false },
  mastra_workspace_edit_file: { enabled: false },
});
 
// Re-enable all tools
workspace.setToolsConfig(undefined);
```

If you’re building higher-level agent flows, this gives you a clean way to harden safety boundaries without juggling multiple workspace instances or custom tool registries. ([PR #13439](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13439 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13439"))

## [Observational Memory Reliability & Introspection Improvements![](https://mastra.ai/_next/static/immutable/media/anchor.3595n93ztlxu8.svg)](https://mastra.ai/blog/changelog-2026-02-24#observational-memory-reliability-and-introspection-improvements)

Observational Memory (OM) gets a strong set of improvements in both introspection and stability.

On the introspection side, core adds `Harness.getObservationalMemoryRecord()`, a public method that returns the full `ObservationalMemoryRecord` for the current thread, including `activeObservations`, `generationCount`, and `observationTokenCount`. This removes the need to reach into private storage internals just to debug OM behavior. ([PR #13395](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13395 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13395"))

```
const record = await harness.getObservationalMemoryRecord();
 
if (record) {
  console.log(record.activeObservations);
  console.log(record.generationCount);
  console.log(record.observationTokenCount);
}
```

On the reliability side, `@mastra/memory` fixes several issues that could bite long-running processes hard:

*   A major OM memory leak that could lead to OOM crashes. The default Tiktoken encoder (often ~80 to 120 MB heap) is now shared across OM instances instead of being allocated per request. This is the primary fix, since previously each request allocated two encoders that could stick around due to async buffering promise retention. It also fixes a cleanup bug where reflection cycle IDs were not cleaned up correctly. ([PR #13425](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13425 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13425"))
*   A PostgreSQL deadlock scenario when parallel agents with different `threadId`s share the same `resourceId`. Thread scope now requires a valid `threadId` and throws a clearer error when it’s missing, plus the DB lock ordering was fixed to prevent lock inversions. ([PR #13436](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13436 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13436"))

If you’ve been pushing OM in production, these changes should translate directly to fewer mysterious crashes, fewer “stuck” workloads, and much easier debugging when you need to understand what OM is accumulating. ([PR #13425](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13425 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13425"), [PR #13436](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13436 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13436"), [PR #13395](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13395 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13395"))

## [Breaking Changes![](https://mastra.ai/_next/static/immutable/media/anchor.3595n93ztlxu8.svg)](https://mastra.ai/blog/changelog-2026-02-24#breaking-changes)

None in `@mastra/core@1.7.0`.

## [Other Notable Updates![](https://mastra.ai/_next/static/immutable/media/anchor.3595n93ztlxu8.svg)](https://mastra.ai/blog/changelog-2026-02-24#other-notable-updates)

*   **Canonical UI state via HarnessDisplayState:** UIs can now read a single snapshot using `harness.getDisplayState()` instead of reconstructing state from 35+ granular events, reducing duplication and inconsistencies across TUI/web/desktop implementations. ([PR #13427](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13427 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13427"))
    
    ```
    import type { HarnessDisplayState } from '@mastra/core/harness';
     
    harness.subscribe(() => {
      const ds: HarnessDisplayState = harness.getDisplayState();
      renderUI(ds);
    });
    ```
    
*   **Workspace instructions overhaul:** Added `Workspace.getInstructions()` and `WorkspaceInstructionsProcessor` so agents receive accurate workspace context, injected directly into the agent system message (instead of being embedded into tool descriptions). `Workspace.getPathContext()` is deprecated in favor of `.getInstructions()`. Also added an `instructions` option to `LocalFilesystem` and `LocalSandbox` so you can replace or extend default instructions per request (for example by tenant or locale). ([PR #13304](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13304 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13304"))
    
    ```
    const filesystem = new LocalFilesystem({
      basePath: './workspace',
      instructions: ({ defaultInstructions, requestContext }) => {
        const locale = requestContext?.get('locale') ?? 'en';
        return `${defaultInstructions}\nLocale: ${locale}`;
      },
    });
    ```
    
*   **OpenAI schema compatibility fix for agents-as-tools + model router:** Tool schemas are now post-processed to ensure all properties have valid type information, fixing OpenAI rejections caused by an auto-injected `resumeData` field producing a JSON Schema without a `type` key. ([PR #13326](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13326 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13326"))
    
*   **stopWhen now receives correct tool results:** Fixed `stopWhen` callbacks seeing empty `toolResults` on steps, `step.toolResults` now reflects tool results present in `step.content`. ([PR #13319](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13319 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13319"))
    
*   **Scorer metadata for Studio:** Added `hasJudge` metadata to scorer records so the Studio can distinguish code-based scorers from LLM-based scorers, and ensured it’s saved across all score-saving paths (evals, hooks, trace scoring, dataset experiments). ([PR #13386](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13386 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13386"))
    
*   **Output processors can now stream during finish:** Fixed a bug where the `writer` passed into output processors during final output processing was always `undefined`, blocking use cases like streaming moderation updates or custom UI events back to the client. ([PR #13454](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13454 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13454"))
    
*   **Safer concurrent workspace file edits:** Added per-file write locking to workspace tools (`edit_file`, `write_file`, `ast_edit`, `delete`) so concurrent tool calls targeting the same file are serialized, preventing silent overwrites during parallel edits. ([PR #13302](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13302 "Visit https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/13302"))
    

That's all for @mastra/core@1.7.0!

Happy building!
